title: Japan Ku-area of Tokyo CPI (November 2026, preliminary) — the release that fixes 11 of 12 months of the 2026 Tokyo yearly average
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its single 17-row HTML table by this session, independently of the fetches that seeded the sibling Japanese entries. Against the header 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks', the row parses exactly as ['October', 'November 20', 'November', 'November 27', ''] — i.e. the Tokyo November preliminary CPI releases 2026-11-27, with an empty Remarks cell. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to every sibling Japanese entry: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page has not been refreshed since 2026-01-23. Release time is not read off this page and is not asserted here.
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-12-25 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and tracked for one measured reason: it is where the second headline of the 2026-12-25 release is actually decided. That release's Remarks cell reads '2026 yearly average of Ku-area of Tokyo' — a figure that is the simple mean of twelve monthly Tokyo index levels, eleven of which are public once THIS print lands, 28 days earlier. Computed on the Statistics Bureau's own 2025-base Tokyo series (e-Stat statInfId=000040491317, fileKind=4, parsed locally out of the OOXML: 680 observations 1970-01 to 2026-08), a December year-on-year surprise of +/-0.5pp, +/-1.0pp or +/-2.0pp moves the 2026 Tokyo annual rate by only +/-0.042pp, +/-0.084pp or +/-0.168pp, and the Bureau publishes the annual rate to one decimal. The twelfth month arrives in the SAME release as the annual average it feeds, so the 2026-12-25 publication carries exactly one genuinely new number, not two — and this date is the last one before it at which the annual figure can still move. This entry is also the direct input to a measured question: how much does the Tokyo December flash differ from the Tokyo November flash it follows? On the BoJ's core measure the November-to-December change in Tokyo's own year-on-year rate has a mean absolute size of 0.20pp over 2018-2025 (n=8, 75% within +/-0.3pp) and 0.13pp over 2000-2025 (n=26) — the longer window flattered by the deflation era, so December is an ordinary month on recent data, not an unusually predictable one. Impact is LOW: symbols is empty, no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI, and this entry's value is calibration and attribution rather than a trade. Registered against FT-japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-12-25-1 (the 2026 Tokyo annual band) and FT-japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-12-25-3 (the November-to-December own-persistence test), both scored 2026-12-26.
